heading: Super 6
paragraphs: Police have widened their investigation into sexual offence allegations against industrialist R Veeramani and two of his associates after identifying multiple victims. Investigators are examining whether the alleged abuse dates back to 2003 and whether vulnerable girls were specifically targeted. The Supreme Court has ordered a fresh investigation into the 2012 rape and murder of a college student in Karnataka's Dharmasthala, widely known as the Soujanya case. A political showdown also erupted in the Karnataka Assembly over the rendition of the national song, *Vande Mataram*, after the state government stopped its official playback following the first two stanzas. All this and more from the South on *Super 6* today with Akshita Nandagopal.
On this edition of Super 6, discussions focus on major political and legal developments across southern states.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay concludes his week-long official tour of the United Kingdom, where the state government signed memoranda of understanding worth twelve thousand three hundred crore rupees, projected to generate over nine thousand four hundred jobs.

Authorities in Bengaluru have busted a major counterfeit medicine racket involving the supply of fake cancer drugs, critical ICU medications, and repackaged expired injections to over 90 hospitals and clinics.

In this India Today Programme Video, anchor Akshita Nandagopal brings you the biggest political and national flashpoints — from the row over Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's UK visit and the DMK's reported 2029 third-front plans to the Mysuru Ganesh Chaturthi procession controversy, the attack on a Kargil war veteran in Gurugram, and the Indian women's cricket team's boycott of the Asia Cup trophy ceremony in Dubai.

This episode of Super 6 covers key national and international political developments. Former Tamil Nadu Chief Minister MK Stalin responds to Chief Minister Vijay regarding an assembly hand gesture while recalling his 1976 detention under the MISA Act.
This edition of Super 6 on India Today, anchored by Akshita Anand Gopal, covers major political developments across India and international headlines.

Political tensions surged in the Tamil Nadu Assembly following controversial remarks and gestures by Chief Minister Vijay referencing the 1975 Emergency, MISA, corruption allegations, and the Sarkaria Commission.

In this India Today programme video, anchor Akshita Nandagopal examines the heated face-off in the Tamil Nadu Assembly over governance, corruption allegations and law and order, with Chief Minister Vijay citing the Sarkaria Commission findings and Enforcement Directorate records against the DMK.
